A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Student-Informed Teacher Training. All 16 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A.1–A.3, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original maze-navigation, quadrotor obstacle-avoidance and robotic drawer-opening experiments, including learning curves, success rates, ablations and appendix perception-awareness measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A.3, including quantitative comparisons and component ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same KL-regularized teacher training, proxy student, shared action decoder and three alternating training phases. The shortened Figure 1 caption does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same color-maze navigation, vision-based quadrotor obstacle avoidance and Franka drawer-opening tasks, with unchanged environments and observation conditions.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 and Appendix A.3 retain BC, DAgger, HLRL, DWBC, COSIL and the unaligned variant. Figure 2 also retains the same maze comparisons. The newly cited related work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.1 retain the same architectures, observations, training budgets and evaluation procedures, including 256 quadrotor evaluations of 1,000 steps. The perception-awareness metrics in Appendix A.3 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the penalty, KL-gradient and shared-decoder ablations and penalty-coefficient sweep. The qualitative behavior analyses and Appendix A.3 perception-awareness analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report success-rate means and standard deviations over three quadrotor trainings and five manipulation trainings. Maze run counts and learning-curve averaging practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results and qualitative findings match, including Appendix A.3. For example, both report aligned-student success rates of 0.46 ± 0.04 in Table 1 and 0.88 ± 0.07 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The performance-gap bound, regularized objective, policy-gradient derivation and Gaussian KL expressions are unchanged. Punctuation edits around equations introduce no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about adapting teachers to student observability, improving imitation and producing perception-aware behavior.

C2.justification: Explanations involving exploration, camera visibility, shared-decoder benefits and residual baseline successes are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-website link under Multimedia Material on page 1. Implementation details and appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Bachman and Precup (2015), Data generation as sequential decision making, with a sentence describing joint primary-policy and guide-policy optimization for image reconstruction. This provides a limited extension of the related-work context.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the Figure 1 caption, replaces Preprint headers with the ICLR 2025 publication header, and makes small wording and punctuation edits. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves slightly upward and its caption is shortened, accompanying the new first-page website line. Minor spacing and reference-page reflow occur; figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves scholarly context by acknowledging related primary/guide-policy work and provides a direct project-resource pointer. These are limited improvements in attribution and resource discoverability; the method, empirical evidence and appendix documentation remain unchanged.
